frames.narration: Normal day: DNS points shoppers at region A (TTL 60 s). Every write is acknowledged in A, then copied to region B about 0.5 s later. B is a warm standby.
At 25 s region A becomes unreachable. The last 7 writes were acknowledged but had not reached B yet. They are the data you lose (the RPO).
Health checks fail every 10 s. After 3 failures in a row (at 50 s) the router declares A dead. Shoppers have been getting errors for 25 s already.
The warm standby is promoted: it becomes writable and its epoch becomes 2. Scaling it up takes 45 s, so it is ready at 95 s.

DNS now points to B, but shoppers cached the old answer. Each keeps using A until its 60 s TTL runs out, so recovery is spread over a minute: half are served by about 99 s, the last by 129 s. That is the RTO.
At 110 s region A comes back. It still believes it is primary at epoch 1, and shoppers with a stale DNS cache are still sending it orders.
Without fencing, A accepts those writes: 170 orders now exist only in A while B has its own history. That is split brain. With fencing, the storage checks the epoch and rejects every write stamped 1.
Failback is a planned second failover: re-sync A from B, make it a replica, then move traffic back in a quiet window. Then run a game day to prove the whole path works.
